notes: Three bills are counted as tax increases without a state revenue estimate because they raise local taxing limits or authority: 2SSB 5313 (school enrichment levies), HB 1590 (lets councils impose the affordable housing sales tax without a public vote) and ESSB 5272 (a higher maximum rate for the voter-approved emergency communications sales tax).

SSB 5581 is counted as a tax increase. Much of its revenue is sales tax buyers already owed that out-of-state sellers now collect after the Supreme Court's Wayfair decision, but it also brought out-of-state businesses into the B&O tax.
SSB 5628 replaced property tax on heavy equipment rental inventory with a new rental tax; its net state effect is an increase, so it is counted as one.
Seven tax cuts passed both chambers in 2020 and were vetoed as the pandemic hit the budget; each veto counts as the governor's no on a tax cut.
Two property tax exemption bills with large state estimates (ESSB 5160 and SSB 6319) are not counted, under the property tax exemption rule.
